The Maddest Swim

By: Diana Lucas | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Extreme swimming is taken to its maddest level, higher, colder than ever before

Summary:
The Big Swim/Mad Swimmers
“You must be mad”

In 2013 renowned cold-water swimmer Lewis Pugh broke the world record when he became the first man to swim in freezing water at an amazing altitude of 5600 meters above sea level in a natural lake on Mount Everest.
If you though that was an achievement….

Now a team of “Mad Swimmers” from South Africa will attempt to break this record and swim more than one kilometer higher than Pugh’s record-breaking achievement.

Led by Jean Craven this team of Mad Swimmers will travel to Mount Ojos in Chile South America and after a challenging 8 day climb up the worlds highest volcano they will cut away the ice with chain saws and attempt to break this record by swimming in freezing water at a remarkable altitude of more than six and a half km above sea level.

The ‘Mad Swimmer’s’, is a group of like-minded businessmen, who teamed up to attempt the craziest swims they could dream to raise funds for charity. The charities they raise money for are various small South African projects, involved with education and/or nutrition because that is where their interests lie. This swim will raise a million rand or over.


Further information:
Accompanying the group will be Dr Sean Gottshack and in speaking to him about it he said this swim will be higher altitude, harder and far more dangerous.
One of the team swimmers is a woman, I met her she’s lovely.

This will not be this teams first such challenge.

Among the latest was from Asia to North America where the team swam from the Big Diomede Island in Russia across the date line to the Little Diomede Island in America.
As a training run for Mnt Ojos the mad swimmers recently swam across the highest body of water in Africa. After climbing up the slopes of Mount Kenya the Mad Swimmers swam across a 4700 m high lake at a temperature of 6.5 degrees.
But at 6 400 Mt Ojs will be a very different story. The climb will take a grueling 8 days with real dangers of bad weather, altitude sickness, dehydration and the climb itself.
On reaching the lake, 400 meters below the summit, they might find it is frozen over and will have chainsaws to cut it open.
Doing an ice swim at this altitude presents many challenges apart from a very real danger of hyperthermia is the combination for the altitude and cold wanting to swim fast to get it done but not able to due to the altitude.
Facing this unchartered territory will be the hardest challenge the mad swimmers will face is not knowing what to expect do to

I have seen some of the footage from the previous swims and it is beautiful and exciting, I would like to propose this story that I will shoot this year in the last week of November and finish it for next year. They can get me to Chile and we can do it on a local budget.

Press Release:


Mad Swimmers
In 2013 renowned cold-water swimmer Lewis Pugh broke a world record by swimming in freezing water at 5600 metres above sea level in a lake on Mount Everest. Now a group of businessmen aptly called ‘Mad Swimmers’ have set out to crush his record. Carte Blanche experiences the gripping and brutal expedition to the Andes to cut a swimming lane into frozen waters at a staggering altitude of 5990 metres. Why? To raise money for charity.


Script:


(NOTE: ALL programme enquiries to go to Ms Kamini Moodley.)


V/O
In 2010 renowned cold-water swimmer Lewis Pugh broke a. world record He became the first man to swim in freezing water at an amazing altitude of 5600 meters in a lake on Mount Everest.

Link
So Lewis Pugh had set the bar at incredible heights that most polar bears would think twice about challenging …5 years down the line another group of extreme sportsmen decided to have a go at breaking this record. Maybe its not surprising they are called MADSWIMMERS.

Jean: “ I can see the bottom of the lake”

Jean: We’ve done amazing swims, the general theme of our charity is to do swims that have not been done before.

V/O
In his day job Jean Craven is a businessman, … he started the MADSWIMMER charity, 7 years ago.

Link
Mad Swimmer’s, is a group of like-minded businessmen who attempt the craziest swims that you can imagine to raise funds for charity in fact they have raised almost 6 million rands is aimed at changing children’s lives.

V/O 8 sec
It was in a swim between Russia and Alaska last year that Jean came up with the craziest of challenges to date.

Jean: One of these Eskimos was pulling me onto his boat said well done Jean what’s up next and in the blink of an eye I said you know what Amos next year we are going to do the highest swim in the world.

Link
After 18 month of preparation and with scant regard for the warnings from family and colleagues the Madwimmer’s set off in late November last year flying to Copiapa in Northern Chile…

V/O 12 sec
Through Chile’s Atacama Desert the expedition travelled into the Andes…. driving up into the mountains until they arrived at Laguna Verde ..a pristine lake 3 500 m above sea level. This was base camp.

Sean : From a logistical perspective first of all I am dealing with a bunch of swimmers never mountaineered before

V/O
Expedition leader, Sean Disney has summited Everest twice and climbed all Seven Summits, for these extreme swimmers there could no better leader.

Sean: We have always been consultants to what I call Mad expeditions, I always have a look at it with no guarantees or promises from a logistical point of view I thought it was feasible

V/O
And with a wind speed of 50km’s an hour at Laguna Verde Rob might have taken the record for the highest kite surfing ever.

Rob :For me not the swim but to help I got my fix with one kite session here.

V/O
Core component of the team was Sean Gottschalk …veteran medic of extreme ice swimmers.

Sean : I have been fortunate to work with ice swimmers what we usually do is essentially treat them like race horses, they protected they rest do the swim and then immediately warm up, this was totally different .

V/O
Darryl Wood , emergency medicine specialist completed the medical team

Darryl: You are really out on your own we did brief the guys on what we could do and we took a lot of equipment up our guides were very heavily laden.

V/O 6 sec
From Laguna Verde the team acclimatized by ascending to higher and higher altitudes.

Link
So what you had here was a group of hardened swimmers hardly scared of freezing cold water but they had to learn a new skill to become mountaineers and forge their own route to their final destination the lake nearly 6 000 m above sea level.

Chris : When we signed on it was the Andes in Chile, a swim in cold water but you don’t think about the actual altitude and as you go to each higher level you are gasping for breathe,

Evan: You know when you are carrying a bag 6 000m you taking a step at a time and all of a sudden somebody would come and say let me take the other side of it.

Jean: I measured I night minus 18 degrees you cannot breathe besides the fact there is not a lot of oxygen that cold air burns your lungs, the wind coming over this ice every morning.

V/O
The original plan to have this record breaking dip in the lake at the bottom of the MT Ojos volcano had to be abandoned when information came back that this lake was rock solid ice…. .. Plan B went into operation, one of the local guides had heard about a lake in the volcanic crater of Mt Tres Cruces, 5 909 metres from sea level…this was unexplored terrain.



Sean: There has been some ups and downs strategise re strategise changes every day but that’s what explores to expeditions do. This has been an amazing new journey, finding a lake that’s actually swimmable at this time of year.

V/O
On Day 8 a small team left to recce the possibility of swimming in the lake at Mt Tres Cruces.

Jean: We took a skeleton crew out early one morning, and you start climbing at 5 000 metres and its an ice climb so it’s a strip of snow you have to climb one kilometre up.

Link
The high altitude, the wind, the ice were just some of the challenges they had to deal with but they were spurred on by their goal of the record swim, Can you imagine how they felt when they got to the lake.

Jean: We were quiet shocked to find this lake solid, solid frozen and we walked on with our boots and crampons onto the lake.

Link
The only solution was to cut through the ice. The good news was they had brought chain saws from South Africa, the bad news they don’t work that well at high altitude.

V/O
This was for the always upbeat Jean the lowest point,

Link
Time was running out the Madswimmers only had one day left on the mountain. So the Madswimmers decided to give the frozen lake one last shot…. And started the long hike to Mt Tres Cruces with the team

V/O
The day started at 4 am …. to get to the base of Mt Tres Cruces they travelled in 4 X 4’s on self made tracks: then a grueling 6 hour vertical ascent until the team reached the rim of the volcano at 6 100 m.

Jean: To my amazement I saw a sliver of light blue water and jeez this wasn’t there 2 days before on our scouting trip the ice on lake had started to thaw. We walked around and picked up a stone which is quiet strenuous at 6 000 m believe me and dropped it through and it actually cracked through the ice and wow what a relief.

Herman: You know first you climb a mountain for 7 hours and you see a frozen lake which is pretty cool on the one hand but to think that you have got to swim there is not so cool.

Chris: But we still had to break open a lot of the ice we had submerged ice under water that was flowing and that was about 20 cms that we had to pick out and break open.

Jean: We gave ourselves about 3 hours and we actually managed with picks to get ourselves a decent sized pool you know when I saw the bottom of this lake I knew this was actually going to happen.

Link
Operating in this sort of environment is not easy…you are working in an isolated environment, with no ambulance support, not much possibility of carrying anyone out and its too high for chopper support. So every decision has to be balanced with the very real possibility of a fatality.

V/O
On the side of the lake 2 tents were set up one to act as a warm up tent before the swim. The second tent a portable emergency theatre ready for any post swim emergency.

Sean: What happens with these swimmers is they get colder before they get warmer so their skin is warming up so if they do it to fast their core ..heart lungs and brain…start to drop because the cold blood goes back to the middle that’s critical stage.

V/O
18 months of planning, Eight days camping in the Andes, Climbing inhospitable terrain the equivalent of 7 Kilimanjaro’s the Mad swimmers were finally able to do what they do best .….Evan Feldman was the first to swim in a wetsuit

Evan: I felt very emotional because I knew what it took to get there for the non swimmers and the swimmers I walked outside and I stood at the front of the lake and I put my hands on my eyes and I said the shima and I hopped into the water.

V/O
Milton Brest who turned 61 on the expedition, was determined to swim.

Milton: Your mind is so nb you have to know exactly what you want to do,
if you think too much you will never do it the guides that worked with us they were unbelievable they stood in a row and all came up to me and just hugged me.

V/O
Herman, Chis and Jean swam in only speedos, goggles and a cap, because of the almost frozen lake they used a time limit instead of distance.

Chris: I have a process I walk towards the water and just climb in…once you have got the cold water on your feet and your legs then you just start adjusting getting your mind right and try and control breathing.

Herman: When you are struggling just turn around and look at the blue sky and see where you are at the moment and enjoy it so that’s what I did. I tried to control my breathing and go under the ice but what happens is I can normally hold my breathe for a min and a half but without oxygen you can only do it for 5/6 sec

V/O
Swimming in the freezing water in temperature between 0.5 and 2 degrees…in the highest known lake ever to have been swum in, the Madswimmers achieved a new word record, …Sean was on Lewis Pugh’s previous record breaking swim.

Sean: That was different, we did have to walk to the lake which was a couple of hours but not anything as hard as this. This was a colder swim there was no doubt about it this lake was literally frozen we had to find a place to let the swimmers go in.

V/O
For each and every mad swimmer …. the journey to this record breaking swim was the hardest thing they have ever done, but they did it.

Jean: it’s the highest swim in the world its almost 6 000 m above sea level its an ice swim it was touch and go until the last definitely by miles its been one of the hardest swims we have done.


Promo 1
They call them selves the MADSWIMMERS …. We join them as they break the ice and break a world record in the process, and it’s all for charity.


Promo 2 15 sec
Jean: it’s the highest swim in the world definitely by miles its been one of the hardest swims we have done.

V/O
A group of businessmen create a new world record and its all for charity.

Jean: We took a skeleton crew out early one morning, and you start climbing at 5 000 metres and its an ice climb so it’s a strip of snow you have to climb one kilometre up. Link The high altitude, the wind, the ice were just some of the challenges they had to deal with but they were spurred on by their goal of the record swim, Can you imagine how they felt when they got to the lake. Jean: We were quiet shocked to find this lake solid, solid frozen and we walked on with our boots and crampons onto the lake. Link The only solution was to cut through the ice. The good news was they had brought chain saws from South Africa, the bad news they don’t work that well at high altitude. V/O This was for the always upbeat Jean the lowest point, Link Time was running out the Madswimmers only had one day left on the mountain. So the Madswimmers decided to give the frozen lake one last shot…. And started the long hike to Mt Tres Cruces with the team V/O The day started at 4 am …. to get to the base of Mt Tres Cruces they travelled in 4 X 4’s on self made tracks: then a grueling 6 hour vertical ascent until the team reached the rim of the volcano at 6 100 m. Jean: To my amazement I saw a sliver of light blue water and jeez this wasn’t there 2 days before on our scouting trip the ice on lake had started to thaw. We walked around and picked up a stone which is quiet strenuous at 6 000 m believe me and dropped it through and it actually cracked through the ice and wow what a relief. Herman: You know first you climb a mountain for 7 hours and you see a frozen lake which is pretty cool on the one hand but to think that you have got to swim there is not so cool. Chris: But we still had to break open a lot of the ice we had submerged ice under water that was flowing and that was about 20 cms that we had to pick out and break open. Jean: We gave ourselves about 3 hours and we actually managed with picks to get ourselves a decent sized pool you know when I saw the bottom of this lake I knew this was actually going to happen. Link Operating in this sort of environment is not easy…you are working in an isolated environment, with no ambulance support, not much possibility of carrying anyone out and its too high for chopper support. So every decision has to be balanced with the very real possibility of a fatality. V/O On the side of the lake 2 tents were set up one to act as a warm up tent before the swim. The second tent a portable emergency theatre ready for any post swim emergency. Sean: What happens with these swimmers is they get colder before they get warmer so their skin is warming up so if they do it to fast their core ..heart lungs and brain…start to drop because the cold blood goes back to the middle that’s critical stage. V/O 18 months of planning, Eight days camping in the Andes, Climbing inhospitable terrain the equivalent of 7 Kilimanjaro’s the Mad swimmers were finally able to do what they do best .….Evan Feldman was the first to swim in a wetsuit Evan: I felt very emotional because I knew what it took to get there for the non swimmers and the swimmers I walked outside and I stood at the front of the lake and I put my hands on my eyes and I said the shima and I hopped into the water. V/O Milton Brest who turned 61 on the expedition, was determined to swim. Milton: Your mind is so nb you have to know exactly what you want to do, if you think too much you will never do it the guides that worked with us they were unbelievable they stood in a row and all came up to me and just hugged me. V/O Herman, Chis and Jean swam in only speedos, goggles and a cap, because of the almost frozen lake they used a time limit instead of distance. Chris: I have a process I walk towards the water and just climb in…once you have got the cold water on your feet and your legs then you just start adjusting getting your mind right and try and control breathing. Herman: When you are struggling just turn around and look at the blue sky and see where you are at the moment and enjoy it so that’s what I did. I tried to control my breathing and go under the ice but what happens is I can normally hold my breathe for a min and a half but without oxygen you can only do it for 5/6 sec V/O Swimming in the freezing water in temperature between 0.5 and 2 degrees…in the highest known lake ever to have been swum in, the Madswimmers achieved a new word record, …Sean was on Lewis Pugh’s previous record breaking swim. Sean: That was different, we did have to walk to the lake which was a couple of hours but not anything as hard as this. This was a colder swim there was no doubt about it this lake was literally frozen we had to find a place to let the swimmers go in. V/O For each and every mad swimmer …. the journey to this record breaking swim was the hardest thing they have ever done, but they did it. Jean: it’s the highest swim in the world its almost 6 000 m above sea level its an ice swim it was touch and go until the last definitely by miles its been one of the hardest swims we have done. Promo 1 They call them selves the MADSWIMMERS …. We join them as they break the ice and break a world record in the process, and it’s all for charity. Promo 2 15 sec Jean: it’s the highest swim in the world definitely by miles its been one of the hardest swims we have done. V/O A group of businessmen create a new world record and its all for charity.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Extreme swimming is taken to its maddest level, higher, colder than ever before
metadata.Summary: The Big Swim/Mad Swimmers “You must be mad” In 2013 renowned cold-water swimmer Lewis Pugh broke the world record when he became the first man to swim in freezing water at an amazing altitude of 5600 meters above sea level in a natural lake on Mount Everest. If you though that was an achievement…. Now a team of “Mad Swimmers” from South Africa will attempt to break this record and swim more than one kilometer higher than Pugh’s record-breaking achievement. Led by Jean Craven this team of Mad Swimmers will travel to Mount Ojos in Chile South America and after a challenging 8 day climb up the worlds highest volcano they will cut away the ice with chain saws and attempt to break this record by swimming in freezing water at a remarkable altitude of more than six and a half km above sea level. The ‘Mad Swimmer’s’, is a group of like-minded businessmen, who teamed up to attempt the craziest swims they could dream to raise funds for charity. The charities they raise money for are various small South African projects, involved with education and/or nutrition because that is where their interests lie. This swim will raise a million rand or over.
metadata.Further information: Accompanying the group will be Dr Sean Gottshack and in speaking to him about it he said this swim will be higher altitude, harder and far more dangerous. One of the team swimmers is a woman, I met her she’s lovely. This will not be this teams first such challenge. Among the latest was from Asia to North America where the team swam from the Big Diomede Island in Russia across the date line to the Little Diomede Island in America. As a training run for Mnt Ojos the mad swimmers recently swam across the highest body of water in Africa. After climbing up the slopes of Mount Kenya the Mad Swimmers swam across a 4700 m high lake at a temperature of 6.5 degrees. But at 6 400 Mt Ojs will be a very different story. The climb will take a grueling 8 days with real dangers of bad weather, altitude sickness, dehydration and the climb itself. On reaching the lake, 400 meters below the summit, they might find it is frozen over and will have chainsaws to cut it open. Doing an ice swim at this altitude presents many challenges apart from a very real danger of hyperthermia is the combination for the altitude and cold wanting to swim fast to get it done but not able to due to the altitude. Facing this unchartered territory will be the hardest challenge the mad swimmers will face is not knowing what to expect do to I have seen some of the footage from the previous swims and it is beautiful and exciting, I would like to propose this story that I will shoot this year in the last week of November and finish it for next year. They can get me to Chile and we can do it on a local budget.
